body:
MAINLINE-065 is complete. Inputs are QUESTIONABLE. Payloads are PROJECTION. No qualified hull safety factor. Simjob simjob-20261020t171207-15195c0bf862 exited 0 after 61 s. The copied model matches 063 at the classical-cap anchor within 0.1 kg.

No published test gives an installed Q for thin SR-200 beryllium on CR-III 5056 3/8-1.0 with the processed bond. The only coefficient this hull can carry is 0.33, NASA CR-1457 equation 2.2-14, admissible with that limit: the 1969 unknown-waviness floor from FPL 1810-A (spring steel on resin paper honeycomb) and from FPL 2171 (aluminum and stainless), which was not opened. It is not a measurement of this sandwich. The cap 0.82 is the perfect-face end of equation 2.2-8 and is not admissible as an installed value. NTRS 19730016169 reached 79.8 to 91.2 ksi on 0.020 inch cross-rolled beryllium after yield, on brazed beryllium honeycomb, so it is not an elastic Q. No titanium table was found. The step from 0.82 to 0.33 is the unknown-waviness knockdown of about 0.4. Density and the bond enter only through Ec and Fc inside K-delta.

At Q=0.33, face wrinkling binds. On 063's favorable ramp the realized gamma is 0.635 to 0.643. Concept payloads are -5,926 and -7,069 kg at R 20, and -18,148 and -22,011 kg at R 30, ISA then optimistic. TRL 7 is negative in every case. Face-density factors are 1.180, 1.218, 1.161, and 1.198. Handbook gamma is realized at 0.20. Factors become 2.118, 2.221, 2.080, and 2.181, and the R 30 ISA concept deficit is -97,878 kg. The classical cap still leaves concept short, and it is the only place TRL 7 is positive. A published Q closes none of the gap. T3 still has to measure elastic wrinkling of the actual coupon, with Ec, Fc, waviness, and a specimen count, before any Q above 0.33 can be carried. This card buys nothing. Files pinned. Stopping.
